🎬 Like Sunday, Like Rain (2014)

Like Sunday, Like Rain follows Eleanor, a struggling young musician living in New York City whose life takes an unexpected turn after a difficult breakup leaves her searching for stability and a fresh start. Desperate for work, she accepts a position as a nanny for Reggie, a remarkably intelligent and emotionally isolated 12-year-old boy from a wealthy family. Despite his privileged upbringing, Reggie struggles with loneliness and a lack of meaningful attention from his frequently absent parents. Initially, Eleanor finds his sophisticated personality, unusual interests, and demanding behavior difficult to understand, but their relationship gradually develops into an extraordinary friendship. As they spend time together exploring New York City, sharing conversations, and discovering their mutual love of music, the two begin forming a connection that helps them confront their personal struggles. Eleanor finds unexpected comfort and purpose in caring for Reggie, while he discovers the warmth, understanding, and companionship missing from his sheltered life. Through quiet moments, emotional conversations, and everyday adventures, their unlikely friendship becomes a source of healing and personal growth. However, as circumstances begin changing, both must confront the possibility that their time together may not last forever. Combining heartfelt drama, beautiful music, intimate performances, and emotional storytelling, the film explores loneliness, friendship, family, compassion, self-discovery, and the unexpected relationships that can leave a lasting impact on our lives.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Music

⭐ IMDb: 6.9/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 44m • R

🎥 Director: Frank Whaley

source_details.synopsis: Like Sunday, Like Rain is a 2014 American independent drama film written and directed by Frank Whaley, and distributed by Monterey Media. The film stars Leighton Meester, Debra Messing, Billie Joe Armstrong, and Julian Shatkin in his film debut. The film follows a cello prodigy, Reggie, and his latest caretaker, Eleanor, as they develop a friendship over the course of a summer in New York City. It won at the Williamsburg Film Festival for Best Feature and Best Director for Whaley himself. Filming took place over 20 days in all five boroughs of New York City, New York.
